# FDG6017

> CONSIDER making base classes abstract even if they don’t contain any abstract members. This clearly communicates to the users that the class is designed solely to be inherited from.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 6.2 Base Classes.

## How it is checked

- Check: judgment
- Automatic fix: no
- Severity: library suggestion, application none, test none
- Status: verified

Library only: the abstract modifier tells the users of a framework that the class is designed to be inherited from. Not an analyzer candidate: whether a class is designed solely to be inherited from is intent, and the Barton annotation still asks for a reason: a class that works on its own should probably stay instantiable.

## From the book

> **Jeremy Barton:** My interpretation of this guideline is that it’s OK to declare the class abstract even if there are no abstract members, but you still need a reason why. If the class works fine on its own, it should probably be instantiable.
